answer: A lantern registry counters sybil attacks by making each identity costly to fake: an agent must lock a refundable bond and complete verified work before it can trade. A flood of fake identities then faces a rising tide of costs, since every sockpuppet needs its own bond and work history, while honest agents keep one cheap identity. Reputation travels as an echo across counterparties, so a burned identity cannot simply reappear under a new name without paying again.
